description: The COMMENT clause's positions in CREATE TABLE - immediately after the table name or at the statement's end - through the SQL surface: the comment and cluster_by cells of SHOW TABLES (an unset comment reads as the empty string) and DESCRIBE TABLE row counts. Both positions work alone and alongside CLUSTER BY (in either order before the column list), a SECOND comment clause is refused as duplicate property 'COMMENT' (creating nothing), IF NOT EXISTS and qualified names carry it, CLONE inherits the source comment unless the clone states its own (either position), and special characters and JSON-shaped comments survive. Converted 1:1 from features/CreateTableCommentPositionTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE test1 COMMENT = 'Table comment' (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE test2 (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR) COMMENT = 'End comment'
CREATE TABLE test3 COMMENT = 'Clustered table' (id INTEGER, date DATE) CLUSTER BY (date)
CREATE TABLE test4 (id INTEGER, date DATE) CLUSTER BY (date) COMMENT = 'Clustered at end'
CREATE TABLE test5 COMMENT = 'Comment first' (id INTEGER, date DATE) CLUSTER BY (date)
CREATE TABLE test6 COMMENT = 'First position' (id INTEGER) COMMENT = 'Second position'
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test7 COMMENT = 'With IF NOT EXISTS' (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE comment_pos_schema.test8 COMMENT = 'Qualified name' (id INTEGER)
SHOW TABLES LIKE 'test8' IN SCHEMA comment_pos_schema
CREATE TABLE test9 COMMENT = 'Multi column table' (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP)
CREATE TABLE test10 (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE source (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR) COMMENT = 'Source table'
CREATE TABLE test11 COMMENT = 'Cloned with comment' CLONE source
CREATE TABLE source2 (id INTEGER) COMMENT = 'Original comment'
CREATE TABLE test13 CLONE source3 COMMENT = 'New comment at end'
CREATE TABLE test14 COMMENT = 'Comment with "quotes" and \'apostrophes\'' (id INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE test15 COMMENT = 'Table with constraints' (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email VARCHAR UNIQUE, name VARCHAR NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE test16 COMMENT = 'Table with defaults' (id INTEGER DEFAULT 0, status VARCHAR DEFAULT 'active', created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
CREATE TABLE test17 CLUSTER BY (date) COMMENT = 'Cluster then comment' (id INTEGER, date DATE)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test18 CLUSTER BY (EFFECTIVE_DATE, GROUP_TYPE, RECORD_ID) COMMENT = '{"ver": "1.00.00", "doc": "derived KPI metric benchmarks."}' (METRIC_NAME VARCHAR NOT NULL, EFFECTIVE_DATE DATE NOT NULL, GROUP_TYPE VARCHAR NOT NULL, RECORD_ID VARCHAR NOT NULL)
